belongs_to: Chapter opening: 'Observe the following figures. Figs. (i), (ii), and (iii) are quadrilaterals, and the others are not. Why?' - Fig. (i)
description: Fig. (i): a convex four-sided figure drawn with 4 straight sides, no side lengths, no letters. Vertices (approx. positions): top-left; top-right (a little lower than top-left, so the top side slopes gently down to the right); far right (lower right corner); bottom (lower left of the right corner). Sides: top-left to bottom is the long left side slanting down to the right; top-right to far-right slants steeply down to the right; far-right to bottom is the bottom side rising gently to the right. A small angle arc is drawn just inside each of the 4 vertices (4 arcs in all) to mark the 4 interior angles. Printed caption '(i)' centred below the figure.

belongs_to: Chapter opening: 'Observe the following figures. Figs. (i), (ii), and (iii) are quadrilaterals, and the others are not. Why?' - Fig. (ii)
description: Fig. (ii): a tilted convex four-sided figure (trapezium-like), 4 straight sides, no lengths, no letters. Vertices (approx.): left; top (highest point, upper right of the figure); right (to the right of and well below the top vertex, about level with the left vertex); bottom (lowest point). Sides: left to top is the longest side, rising to the right at about 30 degrees; top to right is a short steep side going down; right to bottom slants down to the left; bottom to left slants up to the left. One small angle arc just inside each of the 4 vertices (4 arcs). Printed caption '(ii)' below.

belongs_to: Chapter opening: 'Observe the following figures. Figs. (i), (ii), and (iii) are quadrilaterals, and the others are not. Why?' - Fig. (iii)
description: Fig. (iii): a concave four-sided figure shaped like an arrowhead / dart, 4 straight sides, no lengths, no letters. Vertices (approx.): top (apex); right (to the lower right of the apex); notch (a reflex vertex pushed inward, roughly directly under the apex and a little above the level of the right vertex); bottom-left (far left, lowest). Sides: bottom-left to top (long, rising right); top to right (short, steep, down-right); right to notch (short, going up-left); notch to bottom-left (long, going down-left). 4 angle arcs: one inside at the top vertex, one inside at the right vertex, one inside at the bottom-left vertex, and one at the notch drawn on its upper side (inside the figure), marking the interior angle that is more than 180 degrees. Printed caption '(iii)' below.

belongs_to: Chapter opening: 'Observe the following figures. Figs. (i), (ii), and (iii) are quadrilaterals, and the others are not. Why?' - Fig. (iv)
description: Fig. (iv): a closed figure with three straight sides and one curved side, no letters, no lengths, no angle arcs. Straight sides: the left side slants (top-left corner down to bottom-left corner, leaning to the right going down), the bottom side is horizontal, the right side is vertical and shorter than the left. The top side is a smooth outward-bulging curved arc running from the top-left corner (higher) down to the top of the right side. So it has 4 corners but one side is curved, hence not a quadrilateral. Printed caption '(iv)' below.

belongs_to: Chapter opening: 'Observe the following figures. Figs. (i), (ii), and (iii) are quadrilaterals, and the others are not. Why?' - Fig. (v)
description: Fig. (v): a closed figure with two straight sides and a curved top, no letters, no lengths, no angle arcs. Straight sides: a left side running from the top-left point steeply down to a bottom vertex (lowest point), and a long right side running from that bottom vertex up to the top-right point (rising to the right at about 38 degrees). The top boundary is two shallow curved arcs (each bulging upward) joined at a small downward notch near the middle of the top, so the top is wavy, not a straight segment. 4 corner points (top-left, notch, top-right, bottom) but the top consists of curves, hence not a quadrilateral. Printed caption '(v)' below.
